framework.summary: The bill requires developers to write no safety framework or plan; the Board only develops best practices.

transparency_report.summary: A federal Risk Board must develop best practices for standard model-card formats; providers have no duty to publish model cards.
transparency_report.quote: standardize formats and processes for publishing model cards with technical details of artificial intelligence systems

incident_reporting.summary: NIST must set up a channel for voluntary sharing of AI security and safety incidents; no one is required to report.
incident_reporting.quote: may voluntarily share information with the National Institute of Standards and Technology on confirmed or suspected artificial intelligence security or artificial intelligence safety incidents

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter reporting window for imminent risks.

third_party_audit.summary: Frontier model providers must give the NSA's AI Security Center access to the model 21 calendar days before release; this is government pre-release access, not an independent audit.
third_party_audit.quote: Not later than 21 calendar days before a provider introduces into interstate or foreign commerce a frontier artificial intelligence model, the provider shall make available to the Artificial Intelligence Security Center

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no employee protections.

registration.summary: Each provider must register a frontier model with a NIST registry before introducing it into interstate or foreign commerce.
registration.quote: Each provider of a frontier artificial intelligence model shall register that frontier artificial intelligence model with the registry established under paragraph (1) before introducing the frontier artificial intelligence model into interstate or foreign commerce.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or containment capability.

compute_threshold.summary: Frontier models are defined by capability, not by training compute.

revenue_threshold.summary: Coverage does not depend on revenue, spending or users.

harm_threshold.summary: Frontier models are defined by serious risk to security or public health, with no death, injury or damage figures.

penalties.summary: A provider that violates the 21-day NSA access duty is fined at least $100,000 per day the model is on the market without the NSA security guidance; the Attorney General enforces after a 7-day chance to cure.
penalties.quote: Whoever violates subsection (c) shall be fined an amount equal to not less than $100,000 per day

effective_date.summary: The bill states no effective date; deadlines run from enactment.

notes: Penalty applies only to violations of the NSA-access duty in Sec. 3(c); no stated penalty for failing to register under Sec. 3(d)(3). The frontier model definition is capability-based and vague. Sec. 3(f) amends the 2025 Intelligence Authorization Act (test-bed); Sec. 5-7 are agency studies and a threat-sharing pilot.
